One of NASA’s longest-tenured spacecraft is quite literally stuck in the past.
Voyager 1 , launched in September 1977 toward the outer planets of our solar system, is poised to achieve a historic milestone on Wednesday: It will be the first human-made object to reach one light-day from Earth. The spacecraft will be so far away , that by the time its light reaches Earth, it will come from the spacecraft as it existed one day in the past. The achievement is one researchers hadn’t planned on , and yet, as Voyager 1 wades deeper into uncharted stretches of the galaxy, it continues sending back valuable scientific information.
“It's just a wonderful happenstance,” Kareem Badaruddin, Voyager mission manager at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory, says of the milestone. “Just as the stars were aligned for the tour of the planets, they're also aligned for this really magical, special thing that's happening for humankind.”
For Fran Bagenal, a planetary scientist at the University of Colorado, Boulder, who began working with Voyager 1 as a graduate student during its earliest years, the occasion is a momentous technological feat. “What's exciting is the fact that we have a spacecraft that was built in the mid ’70s that is still working,” she says. “Storing data on an eight-track tape that’s working on a spacecraft after 50 years—I mean, it’s amazing.”
Even as Voyager 1 approaches its 50-year anniversary next September, and its end of mission perhaps not long after that, the spacecraft is still checking items off its laundry list of scientific achievements. The spacecraft—alongside its twin, Voyager 2—was originally intended to take advantage of a rare planetary alignment to observe the outer planets .
But Voyager 1 kept traveling beyond the solar system and is now exploring the interstellar medium that fills the space between star systems. Voyager 1’s remoteness gives researchers a rare opportunity to study how the effects of the sun ripple even into the interstellar medium—and at what point those effects wane, says Jamie Rankin, deputy project scientist for the Voyager Mission at Princeton University.
Just as both Voyager spacecraft are moving through space, so is our own solar system—only about 35,000 miles per hour slower, Badaruddin says. That means that as the pair continue their journeys, they’re sending back information about the space that our own sun and planet will pass through in about three years’ time.
“We can learn from telescopes and Earth-orbiting observatories, but there's really nothing like having a spacecraft in that environment that's sending us data,” Badaruddin says.
Voyager 1’s unprecedented journey isn’t without challenges. The craft has stayed in communication with Earth far longer than planned and is trekking through regions of space that it was never built to encounter or study. Researchers are helping maintain crucial functions, but they’re now doing so with a full day of lag in communications both to and from the spacecraft, Badaruddin says.
“Light time is really affecting us,” he says. “You factor it in. It’s like having a long commute.” Building new commands for the spacecraft is now a week-long process, for instance, since it takes time to receive data from the spacecraft, analyze it, and create a new command, he adds.
Still, the Voyager team is used to navigating unforeseen circumstances. For decades, they’ve been managing to make do with a dwindling power supply coming from the craft’s nuclear generators. In September, mission operations switched off some of Voyager 1’s devices in lieu of lower-power alternatives, a maneuver the team dubbed the “Big Bang.” The swap, which saved the craft 10 watts of power, kept mission operations from having to switch off another instrument as early as next summer.
Even when contact with Voyager 1 is eventually lost, the spacecraft will leave a lasting legacy—especially for any future such far-traveling missions, should NASA or another space agency launch one. A successor to Voyager might, for instance, have new devices such as a dust instrument to better analyze the interstellar medium or cameras to give astronomers a better view of these distant stretches of the cosmos, Rankin says.
“I would hope that the Voyagers and their reaching interstellar space has taught us the lesson that we've got to just keep reaching for the stars,” she adds.
Every mission must meet its end, though. And Badaruddin’s best guess is that Voyager 1’s could come in the next three to five years, as the plutonium-238 powering it decays further. Once the craft transmits its final signal to Earth, it will still continue its silent tour of the galaxy.
But Badaruddin acknowledges he’s part of a lineage of mission managers who have said that the spacecraft only has a few years left, only to be proven wrong . “The Big Bang was a rabbit we pulled out of a hat. As long as we can keep finding rabbits, we can keep going,” he says. “Don’t bet against Voyager.”

I knew GTA was something special even before my mom punched me in the face.
This was an accident. She’s not much of a gamer, so the controls on the PS5 version of Grand Theft Auto Online are a bit of a mystery to her. She pressed the circle button, and her in-game character swung a giant punch that caught my character right in the head. Blood splattered. My mom cried out. My brother and I howled with laughter. She’d only been playing for a couple of hours, and she was already punching her kids. What a violent nightmare these games were.
GTA has been a part of my life since I was way too young to be playing it. My brother and I, aged 9 and 11-ish, discovered Grand Theft Auto 3 at a cool cousin’s house. We’d sit there, enraptured, cackling like gremlins and passing the controller back and forth every time one of us got WASTED. I remember wondering if video games could ever get more realistic.
Flash forward a couple of decades, and Grand Theft Auto VI releases on Thursday, a game poised to be the most lifelike, expansive title in the series— maybe in all of gaming . (The game apparently has a system for tracking your empathy.) It also has a real chance of becoming perhaps the highest-grossing entertainment property of all time.
People are very excited about this thing, so much so that there’s been hand-wringing about workplace productivity dropping because some 12.5 million people are taking time off to play the game. (It’s me; I am part of the problem. Please don’t tell my boss.)
Does that feel like too much hype for a video game? Not to me. Not when Grand Theft Auto has always been such a presence at very pivotal points in my life. It’s been much more than a flashy violence simulator.
My brother and I were the target demographic for these games. Vaguely inspired by gangster shoot-em-ups like Scarface , the GTA games have long been vehicles for male power fantasies. We got into them because you could run around and blow stuff up. Be chaotic. It was a good place to do that in, rather than, you know, the real world.
We also weren’t always that friendly when we entered adulthood. Lots of siblings aren’t all that close, especially as adults. When you live far away for long enough, phone calls and occasional visits can only do so much. The distance can be hard to close.
That really changed for us during the Covid-19 pandemic . My brother and I lived hundreds of miles apart. As it did for many people, playing games became a way to stay connected . The best conversations usually happen while doing something like chatting on a long drive, going on a walk, or hanging out at the beach. You couldn’t really do that in the endless Zoom parties Covid unleashed upon the world, where you’d all sit there, talking one at a time, not quite making eye contact on the screen.
Grand Theft Auto Online proved to be a rich environment for finding those kinds of activities. I think it’s the closest anything has ever gotten to feeling like an actual metaverse , where you can do just about whatever you want.
If you’ve played GTAO , you’ve probably rage-quit after getting bombed by an adolescent fighter jet pilot dressed like the prison Joker for the eighth time. That’s fair. But my brother and I usually made the mostly unconscious decision not to fight back. We’d just … hang out. Drive around. Watch the sunset. Spend hours in the in-game nightclubs, listening to real-life musicians play hour-long sets made specifically for the game. We’d go to the stores and curate outfits that felt snazzy.
Really, we are just playing dolls. GTA is a sandbox, after all, and it became the perfect space to mess around without worrying about any real stakes.
“We were brothers before, sure, but we weren’t like adult friends,” my brother told me when I asked him about GTA . “This gave us a way to spend time together and really learn more about what each other’s personality really is.”
We’ve made friends with a group in Australia who shared our approach, just hanging out in this vast virtual world and having casual conversations with the people around us. We’ve managed to convince our parents, who have never played games before, to join us. My mom—who once took our Nintendo 64 cartridge of GoldenEye 007 and smashed it with a hammer because she thought video games would make us violent—now runs around with us in GTA Online , pummeling tailgaters’ cars with a baseball bat. Despite the distance, we can spend time together in something that feels close to a real-life hang, one where we accidentally get smacked with the bat sometimes too.
It’s been a blast, and all that time spent in this virtual world starts to bleed over into the real world. I’ve sought out real-life shows of artists on the soundtrack. Sometimes an outfit would feel snazzy enough that we’d later try to replicate it in real life. One of our in-game characters got killed by a mountain lion on the same night a deer in the front yard was eviscerated by a real-life cougar.
Rockstar seems to be acutely aware of this phenomenon. (Maybe not the mountain lion bit.) What GTA does better than any other game series is spread out into the real world in surprising ways. You can see it in their marketing. Rockstar has given exclusive game clips to shows like South Park . The Weather Channel previewed the game’s advanced weather systems . Older games used music to supplement the game, but now GTA VI has become a major marketing tool for artists like Sza and Justice . Having songs in the game can garner thousands of new listeners.
“When this moment reaches enough critical mass, I think we will see this whole new model for entertainment more broadly,” says Joost van Dreunen, a video game industry analyst . “It's a little bit more of an orchestrated effort between what we play and watch and listen to and attend and connect with and share things online.”
GTA VI has excited many people for a long time. It stands to be the single greatest-selling entertainment product of all time. It’s why role-play servers are still running and populated 13 years after GTA V was released. It’s why Rockstar has invested in this creator-driven community and detailed numerous content-capture features coming to the new title. Van Dreunen says GTA VI is more like an “ operating system ” than a standard video game—a hub for people to build off of in unprecedented ways.
Like its longtime player base, the game is also bound to be much more grown up. The worlds of the GTA games have always been critical satires of certain periods. GTA VI seems keenly aware of how it is meeting the present, so much so that alt-right grifters are dedicated to calling it woke .
“ GTA used to be a very much male-dominated audience,” van Dreunen says. “It's very white in so many ways. It's a privileged lens on a lot of these social cultural issues.”
With GTA VI , all these die-hard gamers are about to start a long story where they spend half the time playing as Lucia, a Latina woman who is one of two main characters. (One of my Australian GTAO friends told me she’s very excited that Lucia is in the game, as that means better tattoos and clothing style options for female players.)
“The fans are being examined as much as GTA has historically put a lens on everything else,” van Dreunen says. “They’re pointing a mirror and critiquing the gamer audience itself.”
This feels like a particularly good time to be doing that. My brother and I, plus a billion other people, can’t wait to dive in. Lots of us will probably never be able to put it down.

Salı günü ABD piyasalarında teknoloji hisseleri öncülüğünde satışlar öne çıktı. S&P 500 yüzde 1 gerileyerek temmuzdan bu yana en düşük seviyesine indi.
Satışlarda yapay zekaya yönelik yüksek harcamaların ne ölçüde getiri sağlayacağına ilişkin endişeler ve ABD elektronik istihbarat kurumuyla Apple hizmetlerini etkileyen teknik kesintiler etkili oldu. Bank of America anketinde teknoloji hisselerinde ağırlığını artıran fon yöneticilerinin oranının ekimdeki yüzde 37’den yüzde 12’ye gerilemesi de yatırımcıların sektöre temkinli yaklaştığının yeni bir göstergesi oldu.
Piyasanın odağında ayrıca Jensen Huang’ın ayrılışından sonra ilk kez bilanço açıklayan Nvidia vardı. Şirket satış geliri tahminini yükseltirken, hisse bir ara yüzde 4’e yakın düştükten sonra günü yüzde 0,4 ekside tamamladı. Riskten kaçışla ABD tahvilleri yükseldi, tahvil getirileri geriledi.
Nvidia’nın beklentilerin üzerinde satış tahmini açıklaması teknoloji hisselerine destek verse de, sonuçların yapay zeka yatırımlarına ilişkin endişeleri gidermeye yetip yetmeyeceği sorgulanıyor. Brent petrol ise Orta Doğu’da gerilimin yeniden artmasına rağmen toparlanan arz ve ABD’de yükselen stokların etkisiyle 92,50 dolar civarında geriledi.

Jason and Lucia’s crime-heavy love story fuels a wonder of digital urban simulation.
Just a minute ago, I was shooting my way out of a cocaine deal gone wrong, darting behind furniture for cover. Now I’m sitting on the floor of my home, working through the instructions to construct an Ikea-style coffee table with my partner. A tiny heart with a plus sign pops up, showing that our relationship is stronger for this quotidian domestic effort.
This is the contrast at the heart of Grand Theft Auto VI , a game that seems to revel in both action movie bombast and the mundanities of everyday life for an up-and-coming young criminal couple.
The reimagined and expanded Vice City is still the grand, crude, satirical criminal playground you’d expect after 25 years of 3D Grand Theft Auto games. And that world is as full, detailed, technically impressive, and polished as you would expect after this latest installment received a reported billion-dollar budget and roughly a decade of development work involving thousands of Rockstar staffers.
But it’s the scenes between the over-the-top and somewhat repetitive action scenes that really make this Grand Theft Auto stand out. Almost every explosive gunfight or high-speed car chase is counterpointed by a sublimely dull, lightly interactive moment of mere routine existence: grilling burgers with pals by the water, playing fetch with a random dog, helping a neighbor tune up a car, or joking around over 18 holes of mini golf.
Taken together, the juxtaposition lends a sense of surreal hyperreality to the goings-on in Vice City and its environs. Each of the game’s two sides gives the other a chance to breathe, forming a series of emotional peaks and valleys that stretch across a truly gargantuan amount of detailed simulation and pure gaming content.
Grand Theft Auto VI never lets you get too settled with a budding life of crime or a budding family life. And it’s all the better for it.
A large part of why this works so well is Jason and Lucia, the dual protagonists whose relationship drives the story. While that relationship starts off a bit awkwardly—thanks chiefly to Lucia’s brief prison stint—it quickly develops into a true criminal and life partnership. Both sides of the relationship are driven by a mutual desire to move up in the criminal world and eventually settle down to a legit family life, if they can just earn enough from the next big score.
Of the two, Jason is definitely the duller partner. An ex-military meathead with a ripped body and a dull, affect-free vocal delivery, a decent chunk of Jason’s lines essentially boil down to “Yeah, sure, that’s fine.” While the game struggles to expose a bit of a tender and thoughtful side hiding underneath Jason’s cool demeanor, the writing can’t quite break through the emotionless masculine facade that Jason wears as a semi-permanent mask.
Lucia is much more interesting as a vivacious and amiable Latina eager to grab any opportunity presented to her. The game takes some time to dig into the difficulties of Lucia’s underprivileged youth and highlight her strained relationship with an unreliable mother, helping to add some important depth to her chip-on-her-shoulder journey of self-improvement. And even the boring Jason seems that much more appealing seen through the lens of Lucia’s good-natured teasing and genuine affection.
While Jason and Lucia can and do operate independently—and the game lets you change between them frequently—it’s their moments of togetherness that really stand out. There’s an easy, rom-com comfort to their time together, whether they’re discussing their future on the couch (“I feel like I haven’t done anything normal in a minute”), taking some time for quick romance (the game cuts away before things get too hot and heavy), or laying down covering fire for each other during a firefight (the lack of a co-op mode for these missions feels truly baffling).
There’s a minor relationship simulation component to the game, with a simple “heart level” that can rise or fall based on some basic decisions. Don’t expect a lot of dating-sim style drama, though; as long as you make the completely obvious choices when they’re presented, it’s hard to let the relationship fall apart. That’s a good thing, too, because this is a relationship that’s easy to root for, even when the participants are literally getting away with murder.
In true Grand Theft Auto fashion, Jason and Lucia’s particular way of chasing The American Dream is through a life of crime. Their travels through the criminal underworld start off kind of slow, as Lucia’s begging gradually compels Jason to reluctantly introduce her to the two-bit operators with which he’s found himself involved.
For the first half of the game, the pair are constantly interacting with a rogues’ gallery of new criminal acquaintances, each more over-the-top than the last, and all of them having specific needs that somehow only Jason and Lucia can fulfill. Many of the missions these small-time crooks have on offer end up feeling like the criminal equivalent of errands—drive here, take that, lose the cops, repeat.
And while a few standout characters develop complex interpersonal relationships with Jason and Lucia over multiple missions, most of these early side characters feel like one-note caricatures that can be distilled to a few tropey traits.
It isn’t until the back half of the game that the main storyline really starts to focus on what it does best: integrating Jason and Lucia into a persistent ring of professional criminals working toward bigger and bigger scores. Here, the missions build on each other, with characters going undercover, casing targets, and learning new skills that eventually come together in some truly tense and bombastic heists. These missions also do the best job of showing off the dual protagonist system, frequently shifting the perspective between Jason and Lucia to highlight their different skills and views on how things are going down.
Outside of this core plot, though, many of the missions and side stories in GTA VI make Jason and Lucia feel like side characters in their own story. I found myself beginning to tune out during some of the many missions in which one or both protagonists serve as glorified security props or overpaid getaway drivers amid other characters’ contrived turf wars. And even dozens of hours into the game, there were still missions that felt like tutorials, seemingly built around the opportunity to introduce some new simulation system or control scheme.
Through it all, the game can’t seem to totally shake the style of sophomoric humor that feels a lot less “edgy” today than it did when Grand Theft Auto III hit back in 2001 (for players who are old enough to remember that release , at least). There are countless extended bits where the entire joke seems to boil down to “Man, kinky sex is weird, isn’t it?” or “Hey look, it’s a male penis (or something that looks similar to one).” And the game seems to take particular pleasure in forcing Jason into uncomfortable situations with plenty of T&A, much to Lucia’s good-natured bemusement.
A word of warning for parents: This is a game that definitely earns a hard “M for Mature” rating and shows how standards for that rating have shifted since GTA: San Andreas earned an AO re-rating for hiding a single sex scene amid its legacy code.
There are moments where GTA VI ’s satire cuts a bit deeper. I especially liked a couple of side stories that skewered buzzword-spewing crypto bros and multi-level marketing schemes with some welcome over-the-top excess. Overall, though, the game’s warmed-over one-liner takes on “wokeness” felt about as fresh as jokes about mothers-in-law and TV dinners, without much in the way of thought-provoking statements on society as a whole in 2026.

Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionary
In a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human.
Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”.
AI advances have spurred questions about whether computers can achieve consciousness, with the evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins among those who answered in the affirmative, saying he was “left with the overwhelming feeling that they are human”. Sceptics, on the other hand , argue that there is a vast difference between how a human brain evolves and how an AI system is built.
Cambridge dictionary said the meaning and use of “human” had become more important in the age of the chatbot. Colin McIntosh, an editor of the dictionary, said AI was “changing the way we talk about being human” and had led to the word of the year being deployed to distinguish our work from that of advanced computer systems. “Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking has made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI: from top mathematicians to teachers of young children,” he said. “A recent increase in compounds such as ‘human-made’ highlight how the word has come to distinguish works or qualities of people, as distinct from AI.”
Prof Rachel Adams, an expert on AI governance and human rights at the University of Cambridge, said : “AI brings us back to questions that we’ve asked for millennia: who are we, what does it mean to be human? The answer to these questions has never been fixed or stable, but the act of asking it is something we have in common.”
Other tech-related words were on the shortlist: “agent”, the term for an AI system that can operate – sometimes alarmingly – without human control, and “analogues”, relating to non-digital activities. A non-tech contender was “wholesome”, a word to describe something which is likely to improve your life either physically, morally, or emotionally.
Earlier this month, “mogging” – meaning to outperform or outshine someone or something – was named the Collins word of the year .
Tech-adjacent words also stood out among the new additions to the Cambridge dictionary. “Looksmaxxing”, describing the act of making oneself as physically attractive as possible, which has been associated with the online manosphere , and “aura farming”, another term often encountered on social media, which refers to “the activity of doing things with the intention of showing a personality that people admire and think is attractive and interesting”.
The former UK prime minister Keir Starmer made the news late last year when some social media users wondered “why he was aura farming” with his TikToks ; Andy Burnham also appears to be attempting to master the art after becoming prime minister.

"Human" is the Cambridge Dictionary's Word of the Year — defined as "having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines".
"The growth of AI means it is now necessary to explicitly say 'human' for things that once could only be done by humans," said chief editor Colin McIntosh.
Examples of current usage included actors Scarlett Johansson challenging "an assault on human creativity" and Matthew McConaughey protecting himself against unauthorised digital reproduction of his voice or image.
"The measure of AI's success should be how much it improves human lives," said Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates on learning about the dictionary's choice.
McIntosh said dictionary editors had to be on top of how words could change over time "to reflect what people say and what they write".
His research revealed a four-fold use of the word human since 1900.
"'Man' used to be used in this sense a lot more, but now it is not acceptable to use 'man' to mean men and women," he added.
"Human didn't come into use in Middle English until the 14th Century, from a French word. Shakespeare used it, but after that it was very restricted in use."
There had also been an increased use of compound words such as human-made and human-driven, to distinguish the works, qualities and skills of people from AI.
"Fears about what humans may lose when we outsource our thinking have made us reconsider the extent to which we rely on AI, from top mathematicians to teachers of young children," said McIntosh.

Gates recently made the case for "human reserved jobs" , external , such as caregiving, and reiterated his call for a robot tax to help fund training for people who lose their jobs to AI.
Other examples included the Nobel Prize in Physics laureate Geoffrey Hinton, who has been described as the godfather of AI, who warned "we're creating alien beings. I'm willing to be selfish and choose humans".
Pope Leo XIV has spoken of new forms of "dehumanisation" , external and the "pressing duty to remain profoundly human".

Tesla can restrict where Cybercabs drive and even block owners from reselling them.
There is always a catch. Or in the case of Tesla ’s self-driving Cybercab , several.
Last Friday night, Tesla said it had invited “select customers” to purchase their very own Cybercabs. The two-seat, gold vehicle is unlike any other on the market: It lacks a steering wheel and brake pedals, and is primarily driven by software. (Other autonomous vehicle companies, including Alphabet’s Waymo and Amazon’s Zoox , offer self-driving rides on ride-hail networks , but don’t let people buy their cars.) Tesla’s “ limited release ” will supposedly offer some people (unclear how many) the opportunity to pay $29,900 to take delivery in December.
From there, though, the Cybercab will need constant cash infusions to stay on the road.
The business model raises questions about what people will actually get when they buy a Cybercab. “You’ll never really own the car,” says Ivan Drury, the director of insights at Edmunds. “It’s more like $30,000 to buy into a franchise.”
According to documents posted on Tesla’s website, the vehicle “will not operate” without what Tesla is calling an “autonomy subscription,” a monthly fee that will start at $299. If owners don’t pay on time and in full, their self-driving cars won’t work. If they try to operate the vehicles in areas that don’t support the service—right now, they’re restricted to portions of cities in Florida and Texas—their self-driving cars won’t work. (That area can expand, contract, or “relocate” at any time.)
If owners do anything that Tesla deems “unauthorized or inappropriate,” the company says it can suspend or cancel the subscription—and their self-driving cars won’t work. If the vehicle loses connectivity, the self-driving cars won’t work. (“Tesla is not responsible for carrier, spectrum, environmental, or other external outages,” its “autonomy agreement” says.)
Tesla also reserves the right to make an owner’s car not work at any time: It says it can, for any safety or security purpose, suspend or terminate access to Cybercab tech, or restrict operations by location, road type, weather, or “condition.” This is particularly salient because the Cybercab is also under investigation by US safety regulators , who are trying to understand why Tesla believes the vehicle meets safety standards without so many of the parts and systems required.
For years, automakers have seen increasingly software-dominated vehicles as an opportunity to get drivers hooked on the same special sauce that makes Netflix, Amazon, and Spotify so potent: monthly subscription services . Because these vehicles can receive over-the-air software updates, manufacturers can offer drivers new services as they make them. The upside is high, tech-style margins that keep rolling in, versus the razor-thin ones seen in car-making. A 2024 report suggested that connected-car features could one day be a $200 billion industry.
In some ways, the subscription model is working. Today, some automakers charge extra for remote start, security, Internet connectivity, and advanced driver assistance features. General Motors said it made $2.7 billion in subscription-related revenue last year from fees drivers paid for its OnStar and Super Cruise services.
But some customers have also found the business model yucky, or even offensive. Why charge extra to “unlock” a feature that’s already built into a car? If an automaker can add a new feature at any time, can’t they also take it away? And if they can take it away, what does “ownership” mean? In 2022, BMW told drivers in select countries it would activate factory-installed heated seats for a monthly or one-time fee ; it eventually backed down after public outcry, pledging the company would no longer charge subscription fees for preinstalled hardware. (BMW is still pursuing a subscription model for some features.) “Consumers hate being nickel-and-dimed for subscriptions,” says Drury.
Tesla was an early mover in the subscription feature space and has offered connectivity and driver-assistance features for monthly or one-time fees for a decade. As the company has shifted away from making cars and toward robotics and autonomous vehicles , executives have made clear that charging for services is the future. (Its Robotaxi service currently picks up fare-paying passengers in parts of eight US cities.) So Tesla buyers may be particularly amenable to paying monthly to make their self-driving cars go.
In exchange for monthly fees, buyers will also get access to other services, too, including remote support , roadside assistance, tire, air filter, and windshield wiper replacements, and tire and camera inspections. (The agreement says that list might change, too.) Cybercabs will be able to “travel autonomously, unoccupied to a Tesla service center,” the company says. The fee doesn’t cover insurance.
Cybercab buyers will have other restrictions. The vehicle is for personal use only. Even though CEO Elon Musk has repeatedly said owners will be able to put their vehicles on Tesla’s wider Robotaxi network to make money during downtime, and even has an online interest form for those who want to own and operate their own Cybercab fleets, the current ownership agreement prohibits that. Buyers are also prohibited from selling or transferring their vehicles without Tesla’s written consent. The company “advises against” children under 13 riding in the Cybercab, and prohibits children from riding without an adult present.
In a post on X , Musk showed no apparent compunction about the Cybercab business model, but did say the monthly price for autonomy “is too high.” He wrote that the price should be “more like ~$115/month.”

MyMems, from the creator of SimCity and The Sims, is a new social simulator powered by AI.
Will Wright, the creator of legendary franchises like SimCity and The Sims , is working on a new game — and it’s built around AI. The new title, focused on your memories, is called MyMems . Like Wright’s other titles, it sounds extremely ambitious, giving players a new way to explore worlds they create on their own. “We want to take your autobiography and turn it into a toy world,” he tells The Verge .
The MyMems website describes the mobile game as a “social simulation” with worlds “built from your memories and the people who shaped you.” You can add “memories” to your game, like speaking a short story to your phone, and those memories are generated into pieces you can place on the game’s map. Your worlds can also include AI-powered avatars, which can represent people you know in your life. Ideally, as you play, the planet starts to become a “map of your psyche,” kind of like Inside Out , Wright says. Worlds can be private, but you can also share them with others.
Here’s another way to think of it, from Virginia McArthur, executive producer and GM at MyMems developer Gallium Studios: “It’s a cozy world builder with a really deep social simulation underneath.”
I’ll admit that I don’t totally get it, and it seems like a tricky idea to grasp without playing it. Still, as heady of a concept as it might be — turning your memories into a game world — Wright and team still want it to be fun. “This isn’t meant to be your legacy diary necessarily,” says Anthony Maitz, a product manager at Gallium Studios. “It’s meant to just be something you kind of play around with.” However, Maitz notes that what you’re working toward is a “proxy” of you — a word that seems to be the inspiration of the game’s earlier title, Proxi: Yesterday’s You Tomorrow .
Like other industries, gaming is starting to reckon with generative AI. Early AI virtual worlds created with models from a startup backed by a Pixar cofounder and Google’s Project Genie weren’t experiences you’d actually want to spend dedicated time with, and indie developers I spoke to in March were largely opposed to the technology . But AI technology has taken some big leaps this year with companies like Google , Meta , and Roblox now letting users make games with AI right from their phone, and retro gaming becoming overrun with AI-powered ports of classic titles.
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick said earlier this year that generative AI has “zero part in what Rockstar Games is building” with GTA VI . But even as a recent industry survey indicated that more game developers are starting to use generative AI as part of their job , workers are pushing back against generative AI use , and the technology is at the center of fierce debates over indie game awards .
Many players are rejecting AI outright, and I wondered if the Gallium Studios team was worried about opposition toward MyMems ’ use of AI. Wright says he has three boys at home and that they are all “pretty negative” on AI. He attributes negativity over AI to be toward the meaning of art and authorship and credit, a concern he calls “well-founded.” But he also calls AI an “amazing tool.”
“We’re not making slop,” says McArthur. But Maitz notes that while the team has “been concerned” about a negative response to the generative AI use, they’ve learned that people don’t mind when they use AI in a “ Scribblenauts -y style” for things like having the game make a high school. The team also found that people got “addicted” to a test app with a character creator, including Maitz’s own daughter, who he says “hates” AI. “By making it so that the player is authoring it over and over, bit by bit, it doesn’t really feel like you cheated,” Maitz says.
MyMems , which is set to launch in 2027, will join a growing field of other social simulations, like Krafton’s Inzoi and Nintendo’s smash hit Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream . But none quite have the pull of The Sims , which remains one of EA’s most important franchises. With The Sims , Wright says that many people tried making their real families in the game.
“It was interesting how people really were naturally trying to map this game, which was like a little toy, onto their real life,” he says. With MyMems , that’s what the team is trying to do the “follow-through” on — what if they made the whole game focused on you?
Imagine opening a family scrapbook and the way people and things jump out, Wright explains. “As you go through more and more pages, pretty soon you have this whole little circus of people and events and things from your life.” It’s chaos, he says. “I want something that feels kind of like that.”

Every serious coffee drinker reaches a turning point when they can never go back to the grocery store grounds or burnt mass-chain batch brew of their youth. From that moment on, their counter will become a stage for all kinds of equipment, from the obscenely simple to the outrageously complex. Drinking excellent coffee is as much a hobby as a habit.
Surprise the coffee aficionado in your life with one of these gifts to pique their curiosity the same way it perks their cup.
The selling point of this sleek travel mug is the push-and-sip lid. Press it down once, and it pops open to let you slip from any side of the cup; you don’t need to look down to find the hole, so you can swig without taking your eyes off the road, your book, or the computer. Press it again, and it locks into place to prevent drips and spills. Miir's stainless steel tumbler keeps drinks hot or cold and comes in seven colors; for an extra $10, you can have it engraved.
Hario's V60 Switch Glass dripper merges two coffee brewing methods into one device: filter and immersion brewing. The namesake switch on the base lets you control how long your grounds steep in the hot water you pour in—or you can opt for a standard cup of pour-over by leaving the switch open. Its versatility lets you experiment with brewing methods to your heart's (or tongue's) content.
Breville's electric milk frother heats and aerates milk to make thick foam for cappuccinos, café lattes, hot chocolates, matcha lattes, and more. An induction heating system provides accurate and automated temperature control. The carafe is dishwasher safe, so cleaning up is as simple as using it. Note that the Milk Cafe doesn't make microfoam, so you can't make latte art, but you can make something just as delicious as what you get at a coffee shop.
The beauty of using a glass vessel for pour-over coffee is you can see exactly how much you've made. This carafe from Fellow has an elegant look, an insulating double-glass design, and a silicone lid that eases into place. Dot markers on the side of the carafe act as volume guides; you can brew up to 20 ounces.
For the utmost control when pulling shots, a manual lever espresso maker is a must. The Flair 49 Pro has all the necessary features to help you dial in the variables, including a pressure gauge, stainless steel tamper, drip tray, and a 49-mm portafilter with a redwood handle and two basket options. Learning to pull the perfect crema takes time and practice, and it's a glorious journey for coffee nerds. Note that you'll need a hand grinder or pro-level burr grinder to get the right grind size, as most electric grinders don't go fine enough.
A gooseneck kettle is a must for all coffee freaks, and it really ought to have a temperature-hold button, too. Cuisinart's Digital Gooseneck Kettle has that magic button, keeping your water at the temperature you set for up to 30 minutes. It has the long and slender neck needed for precision pouring, as well as a big belly that holds up to one liter. For smaller households and tea drinkers, see our other recommendations for the best electric kettles .
Making pour-over coffee requires a scale with a sufficiently wide base, while espresso needs a narrow one. Timemore's Basic Mini Model finds a happy medium to suit both. This compact scale with a timer measures 3.94 by 4.49 by 0.62 inches, has a no-slip mat, and is powered by a rechargeable lithium-ion battery.
Know someone who obsesses over excellent coffee and is always on the road? The compact Go Plus from AeroPress makes sure they never have to drink hotel swill ever again. All you need is hot water and you can brew practically anywhere. The AeroPress might even become your preferred at-home method , as it has for our kitchen expert. This model is upgraded from previous designs with a clear press and chamber, and a travel mug to catch all that much-needed java. It comes in black, cream, and pink.
James Hoffmann authored the definitive book on home coffee-making techniques. Lauded as the pioneer of Britain's third-wave coffee movement, some may recognize Hoffman from his YouTube channel , where he reviews coffee-making equipment. (He even starred in a WIRED Auto-Complete video.) His third book, How to Make the Best Coffee at Home , uses full-color photos and unpretentious explanations to help anyone better understand the world's favorite bean.
Beans stay fresher longer when stored in a container that pushes out excess air. That's what you get with the Airscape Classic Coffee Canister and its plunger lid. The large canister holds 500 grams (about - pound) of your favorite beans and comes in nine colors.
No one ever wants to be in a coffee emergency with no decent brew in sight. That's why the coffee aficionado in your life needs this set of 12 single-serve pouches. Open the pouch, hook it around the lip of a mug, and slowly pour over piping hot water. Voilà —the perfect cup. They're compact and stashable in any desk, travel bag, glove compartment, or anywhere else one might need a quick fix.
For the time-strapped coffee lover who wants pour-over quality with the press of a button, there's the Aiden Precision Coffee Maker by Fellow. The company has a well-deserved reputation for making products with high-concept design that don't skimp on quality. This minimalist machine comes in six colors and has settings to make anywhere from one to 10 cups, and a cold-brew option as well.
This is a newly updated version of our overall pick among best drip coffee makers .
For those who drink both espresso and coffee, the Baratza Encore ESP burr grinder is the bean-crushing machine to own. The Encore line has been a long-time favorite among home coffee drinkers, and the ESP is a redesigned version, with a grind wheel that now accommodates the fine grinds needed for espresso, plus an updated burr set that you can remove for easy cleaning or inexpensively replace when it wears out, all without any tools. This is WIRED's pick for best coffee grinder for most people.
The best cold brew coffee steeps slowly over many hours, resulting in a concentrate with that bitterless taste and velvety texture. OXO uses its trademarked "rainmaker" water distribution system (it works like a large showerhead) to get you those luxurious results right on your countertop. Its Compact Brew Coffee Maker includes a stylish glass carafe, a cork stopper for when you pop it into the fridge, and a reusable stainless steel mesh filter. This is our pick for best overall cold brew maker .

Sosyal medyada paylaşılan bildirimlere göre yeni iPhone’ların etkinleştirilmesinde de sorun yaşandı.

Kesinti, son günlerde ABD’de e-posta, hava ulaşımı ve çevrim içi bankacılık gibi alanlarda yaşanan teknik aksaklıkların ardından geldi. Söz konusu olayların birbiriyle bağlantılı olduğuna dair bir bulgu paylaşılmadı.

Nvidia 'nın kurucusu ve eski CEO'su Jensen Huang , görevinden ayrılmasının ardından ilk kez kamuoyuna açıklama yaptı . Huang, Nvidia yönetim kurulunun uygun görmesi halinde CEO olarak şirkete dönmekten “onur duyacağını” söyledi. Ancak Nvidia yönetim kurulu, Huang'ın yeniden CEO olarak atanmasının gündemde olmadığını açıkladı.
Huang, X üzerinden yaptığı açıklamada Nvidia'nın hayatının işi olduğunu belirterek, görevinden ayrılmasının ardından çalışanlardan, yatırımcılardan, iş ortaklarından ve müşterilerden geri dönmesi yönünde çok sayıda mesaj aldığını ifade etti. Huang, yönetim kurulunun dönüşünün hissedarlar, çalışanlar, şirket ve ABD açısından en doğru seçenek olduğuna karar vermesi halinde CEO'luk görevine geri dönmeye hazır olduğunu dile getirdi.
Jensen Huang aynı açıklamada, Nvidia'da herkesten beklenen standartları karşılayamadığını ve özel hayatında ciddi hatalar yaptığını kabul etti. Yönetim kurulu açısından sorunlara yol açtığını belirten Huang, Nvidia yönetim kurulunun yürüttüğü bağımsız soruşturmayla iş birliği yapacağını da söyledi. Ancak Nvidia yönetimi Huang'ın çağrısına olumlu yanıt vermedi.
Nvidia Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Harvey C. Jones , şirketin finansal sonuçlarının ardından gerçekleştirilen yatırımcı görüşmesinde yönetim kurulunun Huang'ın istifasını oy birliğiyle kabul ettiğini ve Huang'ı yeniden CEO olarak görevlendirmeyi düşünmediğini açıkladı. Jones, Huang'ın şirketin davranış kuralları, standartları ve kurum kültürüyle uyumlu olmayan kişisel davranışlarının ortaya çıkmasının ardından başkanlık, CEO'luk ve yönetim kurulu üyeliği görevlerinden gönüllü olarak ayrıldığını belirtti.
Nvidia'da CEO'luk görevini geçici olarak şirketin CFO'su ve başkan yardımcısı Colette Kress yürütüyor. Yönetim kurulu ise kalıcı CEO için hem şirket içinden hem de dışarıdan adayları değerlendiriyor.
Nvidia yönetim kurulu aynı zamanda şirketin ulusal güvenlik ve ihracat kontrollerine ilişkin süreçlerini denetlemek için yeni bir komite oluşturdu . Komitenin başkanlığını Nvidia yönetim kurulu üyesi ve Goldman Sachs'ın eski başkan yardımcısı Suzanne Nora Johnson üstlenecek.
Reuters'a göre bu hamle, Huang'ın ayrılmasının ardından Nvidia'nın yönetim yapısında attığı ilk önemli adımlardan biri oldu. Huang'ın istifası, özel hayatına ilişkin ortaya çıkan bilgilerle birlikte Çin ile bağlantılı şirketlerle Nvidia arasındaki ilişkilerin de incelemeye alınmasına yol açtı. ABD'li yetkililer özellikle Huang'ın eski Megaspeed yöneticisi Alice Huang ile ilişkisini ve Megaspeed'in kısıtlamalara tabi Nvidia çiplerinin Çin'e yönlendirilmesinde rol oynayıp oynamadığını inceliyor. Megaspeed ise herhangi bir usulsüzlük yaptığını reddediyor.
Wall Street Journal'ın aktardığı bilgilere göre ABD Menkul Kıymetler ve Borsa Komisyonu (SEC) da Nvidia hakkında bir inceleme yürütüyor. İncelemenin kapsamı henüz netleşmiş değil; ancak şirketin yatırımcılara yaptığı açıklamaların yanıltıcı olup olmadığının değerlendirilen konular arasında olduğu belirtiliyor.
Öte yandan Huang'ın yeniden göreve getirilmesi için çalışanlar, yatırımcılar ve teknoloji dünyasından isimlerin destek verdiği bir kampanya da yürütülüyor. Huang'ın kendisi de dönüşe açık olduğunu açıkça ortaya koymuş durumda. Buna rağmen Nvidia yönetim kurulunun son açıklaması, şirketin şimdilik Huang sonrası döneme ve yeni bir kalıcı CEO arayışına odaklandığını gösteriyor.

Osmo’s smell model is already being used in the fragrance industry. But are medical diagnostics and threat detection a sniff too far?
In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.”
“Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.”
In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating between smells, and about as good as a junior perfume designer at creating them. It says its technology is already being used in the fragrance industry to help brands design and manufacture new scents. Last month, the company says, Osmo’s AI model outperformed in-house perfumers at one of the world’s largest consumer goods companies. Wiltschko believes it could be deployed eventually for threat detection at airports, for example, or diagnosing diseases.
Wiltschko spun the startup out of his work at Google Brain, the search giant’s former AI research lab, in 2023, and he is running the same playbook as AI startups in other domains: Throw a lot of data at difficult problems, and see what happens. The challenge with scent, Wiltschko says, is that there was a dearth of good data. Before Osmo, there were fewer than 200,000 human descriptions of smells in existing databases, by his count. Plus, the chemical sensor devices needed to collect data are expensive, and the fragrance industry is secretive about its work on olfactory science.
A lot of the company’s work has been in creating its own dataset of more than 10 million human labels and 800 million “scent tokens,” which describe the exact molecules and concentrations that go into creating specific odors. Osmo uses spectrometers and other chemical sensors, running around the clock, to break down the molecular makeup of everything from fruit and flowers to pantry staples and organs. A team of around 70 trained data labelers in the US and overseas spend their days sniffing things and writing down what they smell like, using a standardized fragrance vocabulary.
Mapping out scents in this way is throwing out some unlikely parallels. In the same way that changing the order of words can drastically influence the meaning of a sentence, rearranging scent molecules in different proportions can drastically alter the smells humans perceive. “The scent tokens that define the smell of a newborn baby have massive overlap with the scent tokens in a fresh plate of cooked spaghetti,” Wiltschko says. (Specifically Barilla brand spaghetti, he says, which perhaps raises some questions for the people at the pasta factory.)
The company also creates its own scents, using a smell-printing robot the size of a school bus that mixes ingredients according to precise formulas to make samples for Osmo’s own research and fragrances for paying customers. It can design and print scents to order based on a ChatGPT-style prompt. Wiltschko flipped open his laptop to show me how the AI model worked. He opened a text box on screen, and I asked him to generate a fragrance that smelled like a Portuguese custard tart (we were in Lisbon for Web Summit), aimed at 18- to 23-year-old men. The system spent a few minutes cogitating, then generated three options for potential scent profiles that matched the brief (creamy, coconutty, fruity) and the molecules needed to create them. If I’d continued with the ordering process, my signature L’Eau de Custard would have been ready about a week later.
Osmo’s technology has already been used to create retail fragrances, including for giants like Procter & Gamble. The Gates Foundation, which invested $5 million when Osmo launched, later gave the company a $3.5 million grant to assess molecules that repel disease-carrying insects, and Osmo identified eight substances that were more repellent than DEET. Osmo has also worked with StockX, the online clothing marketplace, on using smell to spot counterfeit sneakers by detecting differences in the chemical composition of the materials used in the shoes.
But not everyone is convinced by the technology or the company’s big claims. Avery Gilbert, a smell scientist and author of What the Nose Knows , has been sharply critical of Osmo on his Substack , arguing that some of its marketing claims are undocumented, and that its patent filings still rely on human sensory panels and perfumers, rather than AI. “This heavy reliance on human sensory judgments seems odd for a company premised on super-cool AI,” he wrote in March. A representative for Osmo did not respond in time for publication.
Michael Schmuker, a former professor of neural computation at the University of Hertfordshire who has previously consulted for Osmo, says the company’s technology is an achievement. With colleagues, he created an open-source, reverse-engineered version of Osmo’s 2023 model, but it lacks the reams of data the company has collected since.
But even with all this smell data, Osmo may be missing some of the factors that make human olfaction unique, Schmuker says. “Smell is super complex. Context is very important for smell. The same molecule may evoke a different association depending on context,” he says. “[The smell of] a French cheese like Camembert is partly the same molecule as in used nappies. You don’t confuse the two because of the context.”
In a controlled setting like a fragrance lab, this lack of context may not matter so much. But it could have an impact if Osmo’s technology becomes, as Wiltschko suggests, the “olfactive channel” for AI world models. Imagine a machine that could sniff out spoilage in food on a production line, or detect tumors through smell the way dogs have been trained to do in pilot studies .
For that to happen, sensor technology will need to get a lot better, Schmuker says. The models will need to keep improving. Medical diagnostics is the biggest prize.
“There’s a lot of history of companies that have gone directly at that mountain peak and, unfortunately, not been successful, because it is very expensive and it is very difficult,” Wiltschko says. "So what we’re doing is building this foundation at the foothills of all these mountains. We’re sending expeditions up to the mountains, doing explorations, and basically smelling the whole world.”

The technologies could make IVF more effective and accessible. But they’re also raising difficult ethical questions about how far reproductive medicine should go.

Türkiye İstatistik Kurumu ( TÜİK ) verilerine göre, işsiz sayısı 2026 Temmuz-Eylül döneminde 2025'in aynı dönemine göre 46 bin kişi artarak 2 milyon 870 bin kişi oldu. Mevsim etkisinden arındırılmış işsizlik oranı 0,1 puanlık artışla yüzde 8,1 seviyesinde gerçekleşti.
TÜİK'in resmi internet sitesinde yer alan yazılı bültende, "Hanehalkı İş Gücü Araştırması sonuçlarına göre; 15 ve daha yukarı yaştaki kişilerde işsiz sayısı 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe göre 46 bin kişi artarak 2 milyon 870 bin kişi oldu. İşsizlik oranı ise 0,1 puanlık artış ile yüzde 8,1 seviyesinde gerçekleşti. İşsizlik oranı erkeklerde yüzde 6,8, kadınlarda yüzde 10,7 olarak tahmin edildi" denildi.
İstihdam edilenlerin sayısı 2026 yılının üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe kıyasla 62 bin kişi azalarak 32 milyon 434 bin kişi, istihdam oranının ise 0,3 puanlık azalış ile yüzde 48,3 oldu. Bu oran erkeklerde yüzde 65,7 iken, kadınlarda yüzde 31,4 olarak gerçekleşti.
İş gücü, 2026 yılının üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe göre 17 bin kişi azalarak 35 milyon 304 bin kişi, iş gücüne katılma oranı ise 0,2 puanlık azalış ile yüzde 52,6 olarak belirlendi. İşgücüne katılma oranı erkeklerde yüzde 70,5, kadınlarda ise yüzde 35,1 oldu.
15-24 yaş grubunu kapsayan genç nüfusta işsizlik oranı bir önceki çeyreğe göre 0,1 puanlık artış ile yüzde 14,1 oldu. Bu yaş grubunda işsizlik oranı erkeklerde yüzde 10,4, kadınlarda ise yüzde 21,3 olarak tahmin edildi.
Mevsim etkisinden arındırılmış istihdam edilenlerin sayısı 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe göre tarım sektöründe 58 bin kişi, sanayi sektöründe 133 bin kişi azalırken inşaat sektöründe 9 bin kişi, hizmet sektöründe 120 bin kişi arttı. İstihdam edilenlerin yüzde 13,6'sı tarım, yüzde 19,3'ü sanayi, yüzde 6,8'i inşaat, yüzde 60,3'ü ise hizmet sektöründe yer aldı.
İstihdam edilenlerden referans döneminde işbaşında olanların, mevsim ve takvim etkilerinden arındırılmış haftalık ortalama fiili çalışma süresi 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe göre değişim göstermeyerek 42,3 saat oldu.
Zamana bağlı eksik istihdam, potansiyel işgücü ve işsizlerden oluşan atıl işgücü oranı 2026 yılı üçüncü çeyreğinde bir önceki çeyreğe göre 1 puanlık artış ile yüzde 30,9 oldu. Zamana bağlı eksik istihdam ve işsizlerin bütünleşik oranı yüzde 20,5 iken işsiz ve potansiyel işgücünün bütünleşik oranı yüzde 20,2 olarak tahmin edildi.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are holding talks in Shenzhen, a day before a one-of-its-kind trilateral summit with US President Donald Trump in the southern Chinese city.
Chinese and Russian news agencies reported that the two leaders began talks around midday on Wednesday.
It was their fifth meeting this year, one of which took place by video link.
Thursday’s meeting has raised concern in Kyiv and European capitals that the three leaders could settle Ukraine’s future without them and divide the world into modern spheres of influence.
Washington initially said Ukraine was not expected to be on the agenda, but Trump later said it would be. Xi regards the war as not China’s concern.
Beijing has said only that the leaders will hold “in-depth exchanges on safeguarding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major-power relations” on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting.
According to Washington, the Iran war and nuclear disarmament are also on the table after the US-Russia bilateral nuclear weapons treaty expired in February. China has long argued that the US and Russia should cut their much larger arsenals before it will discuss limits on its own.
Opening the event, Xi called for stronger international cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade. China would pursue “deep-seated reform”, he said, starting with lower tariffs, wider market access and work on regulation and management standards.
Putin, who has been shunned by the West since he invaded Ukraine in 2022, told the APEC gathering he expected the trilateral to be “highly useful”.
With military and political risks rising, he said, “what is desperately needed is unity rather than division... and dialogue rather than ultimatums.”
He also argued that Western sanctions had failed, saying they could not fully halt growth or wreck the economies of rival states.
Trump was still in the Philippines on Wednesday, where he attended a summit of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN). A day earlier he met fellow Quad leaders from Australia, Japan and India for the first time in his second term. The group is broadly seen as a counterweight to Chinese influence in the region.
He said he hoped to hold one-on-one talks with both Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un in Shenzhen, adding that Kim “would like” to meet in China.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Manila, stopped short of confirming a Kim meeting but said engagement was the only way to resolve problems with North Korea.
Around 2,000 people protested during Trump’s visit, carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica”, a reference to a US supply chain initiative.

Democrat Mary Peltola flipped the US Senate seat in Alaska on Tuesday after a tight race that unseated Republican incumbent Dan S. Sullivan, according to the official ballot count.
With 50.12% of the vote, Peltola's win means the US Senate will have a 56-44 Democratic majority, clinching the chamber's last open race in a midterm election that crushed Republicans across the country and handed US President Donald Trump a firm rebuke of his second term.
"As our next United States Senator, I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families," Peltola said in a statement late on Tuesday.
"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honour than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs and put Alaska first."
With far-flung rural voters in remote villages, the vote count in Alaska took two weeks to complete, but offered Peltola a strong mandate.
With 144,302 votes, Peltola beat Sullivan's 131,844 votes, even when combined with a second candidate named Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. who earned 4,760 votes.
Trump had called for another Republican candidate in the race, Gerald Heikes, to have his votes "immediately given" to Dan S. Sullivan, calling it the "fair solution."
Heikes won 6,105 votes in the race, but merging all the votes that Trump wanted to combine would still not have been enough to beat Peltola.
The Alaska Senate race had attracted national attention following a New York Times investigation revealing that aides to Peltola had recruited another man named Dan Sullivan to run for office with the goal of siphoning votes from the Republican incumbent.
"My opponent's campaign is literally focused on misleading Alaskans, lying and cheating," Senator Sullivan told reporters in Anchorage on election day.
The fact that there were two candidates named Dan Sullivan had repeatedly drawn the ire of Trump, who said Democrats had used a "decoy" to siphon votes from the Republican candidate.
The Trump administration had gone so far as to ask the courts to block certification of the results if the incumbent Sullivan lost because of the potential mix-up.
The legal bid, which Trump has said he ordered personally, sparked alarm in political circles, but was dismissed by a federal judge ahead of the election.
However, US Attorney Michael Heyman claimed federal investigators were conducting both criminal and civil probes involving the Alaska Senate race.
Peltola's historic victory makes her one of the first two Native American women ever to be elected to the US Senate, where she will join Minnesota Senator-elect Peggy Flanagan.
Democrats will control 56 seats in the 100-seat Senate which will give them the power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump's administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.

Mary Peltola defeated the state's Republican incumbent after a controversial race
Democrat Mary Peltola has won Alaska's hard-fought Senate race, completing a sweeping victory for the party in the US upper house in the midterm elections.
The win gives the Democrats a 56th Senate seat following a tumultuous and controversial election in Alaska, which featured alleged spoiler recruitment efforts and unprecedented court battles.
It took two full weeks of counting to call a winner in the 3 November poll due to the logistical challenge of collecting ballots from across the state's remote expanse.
It is the ninth Senate seat the Democrats have taken from Republicans in the midterms, giving the party control of the US Congress for the last two years of Donald Trump's presidency.
The Democrats also won back the House of Representatives, the lower chamber.
Peltola defeated the incumbent Republican senator, Dan S Sullivan, who is yet to comment.
In her victory statement, Peltola said the "status quo in DC is not working for Alaska".
She recalled speaking to "elders in tears about empty fish racks" and to parents in rural Alaska choosing between heating their homes and putting food on the table.
Peltola is the first Alaska Native elected to the US Senate, and is the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in Alaska since 2008.
Donald Trump won the state by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but defeat for the Republicans in this year's US Senate race in the state caps off a string of losses in the midterms for the president's party.
Many voters across the United States cited cost-of-living issues as a factor that affected how they cast their ballots.
Trump says Alaska voters chose the wrong Dan Sullivan. What does the data show?
Could Alaska's fishing industry tilt Washington's balance of power?
Peltola's campaign had come under fire after the New York Times , external reported that her team worked with people who tried to recruit so-called spoiler candidates in an alleged attempt to confuse voters.
The alleged scheme led to a candidate named Daniel J Sullivan - a complete political unknown residing in a small coastal town who shared a name with the state's current US Senator and incumbent, Dan S Sullivan - contesting the race.
After legal challenges, state courts ruled that Daniel J Sullivan could remain on the ballot, and election officials distinguished them on election materials.
Peltola denied having knowledge of the alleged plot but her campaign swiftly came under fire, and both the US justice department and Alaska's Republican governor said they would launch investigations.
The Trump administration also filed a lawsuit attempting to stop the certification of the election results if the incumbent Republican Senator Sullivan lost.
A federal judge, though, dismissed the case, following legal challenges from Alaska election officials as well as the Peltola campaign and voting groups.
Due to Alaska's ranked-choice voting system, voters confused about which Dan Sullivan was the incumbent could have simply chosen both men, listing them as their first and second choices.
If they did so, after the first round of voting was complete, tabulation would have re-allocated any votes from Daniel J Sullivan - who stood little to no chance of winning - to Dan S Sullivan.
Experts told the BBC that this process made it difficult for any potential spoiler candidate to have any impact on the results.
An analysis by BBC Verify found that even if every vote for Daniel J Sullivan had gone to the incumbent, Dan S Sullivan, Peltola would still have won.
The Democratic win in Alaska cements the party's majority in the US Senate, as the party now has 56 seats to the Republicans' 44.
The most senior Democrat in the Senate, Chuck Schumer, said Peltola had run "a pitch-perfect campaign devoted to the issues Alaskans care most about". Hailing the Democrats' final tally in the Senate, he said: "56 seats was an unimaginable result even just a few months ago."
The Alaska seat was initially one of several toss-up races that appeared as a must-win for Democrats if they wanted to gain control of the US Senate. But by the time Peltola was called the winner, they had seats to spare.
With 99% of ballots counted, Peltola had slightly more than 50% of the votes, while Sullivan trailed on less than 46%.
Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general and an ally of Trump, campaigned on his record of delivering energy and military investment for the state.
Peltola promised Alaskans a more independent voice in Washington.
"As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my life to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," she said in her victory statement.
"I will stand up to anyone to take on the rigged system in DC and deliver results for Alaska's working families."

Watch: Jeff Bezos on involvement in casting Robert Pattinson as James Bond
Jeff Bezos has said he was "heavily involved" in casting Robert Pattinson as the new James Bond.
Speaking at an event in California, the Amazon chairman said he was originally "biased against" Pattinson - who starred in many blockbuster films like Batman and the Twilight series - "because he's already so famous".
The role of 007 has typically gone to an actor who is not as well known at the time of casting. But Bezos said in screen tests, "it was so obvious he is James Bond".
This will be the first 007 film in the official series not under the creative control of the Broccoli family, who had overseen the franchise since the first movie in 1962. Amazon purchased MGM, which co-owns the franchise, in 2022.
'Good Bond vibes' - Hollywood locals react to Robert Pattinson cast as new 007
"There was something special about Rob", Bezos said at Semafor Silicon Valley & The World Event on Tuesday.
Pattinson was unveiled as the franchise's seventh James Bond on Monday, taking over from actor Daniel Craig. He will star in the 26th Bond movie, due to be released in 2028.
In a statement, the London-born actor said: "James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime."
The next Bond film will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, but its title and exact release date have not yet been announced.
The announcement comes after years of intense speculation about who will take over from Craig in one of the most high-profile - and highly scrutinised - roles in entertainment.
Robert Pattinson was unveiled as the franchise's seventh James Bond on Monday
Several other actors, including Josh O'Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden, were reported to be in the frame for the role as screen tests took place in recent weeks.
But Amazon MGM ultimately went with a household name, choosing a more bankable movie star who is widely seen as a safe pair of hands.
"We ran a really tight process and made the final decision on Friday," Bezos said.
There were five finalists who went through "real, old-fashioned screen tests", acting out three different scenes in full costume, with real sets and other actors, he said.
"By the time we got to this list of five, they were all amazing. But there was something special about Rob and his performance," Bezos added. "It was immediately un-debated. Denis [Villeneuve], the director … we all gravitated toward Rob."
The pick comes amid widespread Hollywood cuts and consolidation, with studios struggling to get people into cinemas.
Hollywood insiders have said Pattinson was viewed as a safe pick to bring audiences in, rather than taking a risk on a new actor who could grow with the franchise.
"Maybe he's boring. Maybe Hollywood would be passing up a chance to anoint a badly needed new star. But with so much at stake for everyone involved, that all makes him the obvious pick," Hollywood journalist Matthew Belloni, who predicted the pick, wrote in his newsletter.

A further extension of an enrichment facility in North Korea has been "externally complete" since last month, UN nuclear watchdog head Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday.
Inspectors of the International Atomic Energy Agency ( IAEA ) have not had access to North Korea since 2009, with the agency relying on satellite imagery and open sources to monitor the country's nuclear programme.

Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea
The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.
Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen , said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”
She expressed confidence all 27 member states would stand behind the loan, despite four central and eastern European countries having already ruled themselves out.
The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, said he hoped for the swift adoption of the loan and was counting on the support of all EU member states: “Strong support for Ukraine is the best signal to Russia that this war must end,” he wrote on X.
Zelenskyy convinced EU leaders last month that his country faced a €70bn funding gap in 2027 . The EU pledged to cover €45bn and wants Ukraine’s other allies to cover the rest.
Only 11 months ago, the EU agreed a €90bn loan for Ukraine, which was intended to cover two-thirds of Kyiv’s military and civilian needs in 2026 and 2027. But as Russia’s attacks have escalated , the cost of Ukraine’s defence and the toll of economic disruption continue to rise.
Andrius Kubilius, the EU defence commissioner, said Ukraine’s military spending was increasingly dominated by drones. Ukraine, he told reporters, expected Russia to use 10m drones this year and 20m in 2027. “Ukraine with EU assistance needs to match – and will match,” he said.
The EU loan is split into two parts: €25bn for weapons and €20bn for civilian needs, including funding essential services, such as schools and hospitals.
Von der Leyen expressed confidence that all member states would support the loan because “all 27 member states say very clearly that they want to support Ukraine”. She said member states could choose to support Ukraine’s civilian needs, rather than military spending.
Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria, however, have said they do not intend to take part in the latest funding round for Ukraine, prompting a warning from the German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, that he would block the EU’s seven-year budget unless all countries got onboard.
The four central and eastern countries are net beneficiaries of the EU budget, while Germany is the largest payer and Ukraine’s biggest EU donor.
The EU wants Ukraine’s non-EU allies – such as Norway, the UK and Canada – to find €25bn for Kyiv in 2027.
The EU proposal included provisions “to help other countries to help us”, a senior commission official said. Brussels has proposed that G7 countries that provide new loans get guarantees that the borrowing can be repaid with future profits from Russia’s frozen assets.
The profits from the Russian assets are being used to repay a €45bn loan issued by the G7 to Ukraine in 2024.
Countries with a triple-A credit rating could opt to provide guarantees to the EU budget up to €5bn to expand European borrowing for Ukraine on capital markets. The commission has identified six countries that fall into this category: Australia, Canada, Liechtenstein, Norway, Singapore and Switzerland.
EU officials previously said the UK and other allies needed to do more to support Ukraine in 2027, arguing that the EU was shouldering too much of the burden. The UK subsequently pledged a £10bn economic and military support package for Ukraine.
Zelenskyy said: “The UK, Canada, Japan, and Norway have been helping tremendously in our defence of life, and establishing clear rules under which they can provide further aid in conjunction with the EU will help even more.”
